tutorial.title: Welcome to GeoChase
tutorial.step1Content: Use the drawing tools to create circles, lines, points, and polygons on the map.
tutorial.step2Content: Save your work as projects and load them later.
tutorial.step3Content: Search for places and use coordinates in your drawings.
tutorial.projectionHelp: Choose a projection when creating a project, or open Project Settings from the Projects menu to change it later. Mercator keeps drawn lines straight on the map; Geodesic (WGS84) follows the shortest paths over the curved Earth, so lines can appear curved. The basemap is selected separately in the top toolbar. The projection applies to the whole project and is saved in the project and JSON exports. In image mode, measurements use the image plane and its calibrated scale.

intros.interface: Explore the main controls, workspace settings and map panel.
intros.tips: Keyboard shortcuts and practical tips for your mapping workflow.

cards.workspaceContent: The top bar contains the main tools. Open Build for advanced line tools.
cards.interfaceContent: Use the top-right menu to change themes and language or open the project repository.
cards.drawingContent: Create points, circles, lines, routes and polygons with advanced construction tools.
cards.searchContent: Search from the top bar and choose a basemap from the selector on the right.
cards.pathContent: Find places within a chosen distance of a route.
cards.elevationContent: Review terrain and elevation along line segments.
cards.pointsContent: Manage coordinates and reuse points as geometry centers.
cards.projectsContent: Save work, choose a projection and export GPX files.
cards.assistantContent: Ask for places, constructions or image calibration in plain words, with ready-to-try examples.

address.item1: Enter a place name or address in the search box. This search is hidden in image mode.
address.item2: Choose a result to center the map on that location.
address.item3: Use the result actions to create a point or a circle at that location.

alongPath.title: Search along a route
alongPath.item1: Open Nearby places from a line, route or point menu.
alongPath.item2: Set the distance band around the selected route or point.
alongPath.item3: Filter results by category, name or elevation, then select a result to inspect it.

ruler.item1: Open the round Tools button on the map and choose the ruler.
ruler.item2: Set the start and end points; distance and azimuth update as you move. Click to finish, or press Escape to cancel without adding a layer.

add.item1: Open an item’s ⋮ menu and choose Add a note to attach a note to it.
add.item2: Use the Note button in the top toolbar to create a free note.
add.item3: Enter a title and the note text.
add.item4: For a free note, choose the shape or map item it refers to, if applicable.
add.item5: Hover over a note marker to preview its content.

manage.item1: Choose Point in the top toolbar, or right-click the map to create one.
manage.item2: Enter coordinates or select a saved point as the location.
manage.item3: Give the point a name; GeoChase can suggest one automatically.
manage.item4: Find saved points in the notebook, where you can edit or delete them.

pdf.item1: Open a project, then use PDF in the top toolbar to add or view its document.
pdf.item2: Select a PDF file (up to 50 MB) to open it in the viewer.
pdf.item3: Use the viewer controls to change pages, zoom, fit, rotate, show thumbnails or download.
pdf.item4: Resize the viewer from its left edge; enter the password if the PDF is protected.
pdf.item5: The PDF password is stored locally in this browser.
pdf.item6: Use the trash button to remove the PDF from the project.
pdf.item7: PDFs belong to the current project and are not included in JSON exports.

toolbar.title: Top toolbar
toolbar.content: The first row contains search, Projects, help and the More menu. The second row contains drawing tools and the basemap selector.
toolbar.item1: Point, Circle, Line, Route and Polygon open their creation forms.
toolbar.item2: Open Build for Azimuth, Intersection, Parallel, Free Hand and Line at Angle.
toolbar.item3: Note creates a note; PDF imports or opens the project document.
toolbar.item4: The selector on the right offers Geoportail (IGN), OpenStreetMap and Google map, satellite and terrain layers.
toolbar.item5: Use the small arrow below the toolbar to collapse or reopen it.

moreMenu.title: More menu: themes, language and GitHub
moreMenu.content: The three-dot menu in the top-right corner contains workspace settings.
moreMenu.item1: Themes offers 14 palettes. Your choice is remembered.
moreMenu.item2: Language switches the app between French and English.
moreMenu.item3: GitHub opens the project repository in a new tab.

sidebar.title: Sidebar and map
sidebar.content: The button at the middle of the left edge shows or hides the layers notebook. Map zoom controls are at the bottom-right; the round tools button below them opens the measuring ruler.
sidebar.item1: Use the notebook to manage map items; the map controls adjust zoom and open the ruler.

itinerary.title: Route
itinerary.content: Create a driving or walking route between saved points.
itinerary.item1: Enter a name for the route.
itinerary.item2: Choose saved points for the start and destination.
itinerary.item3: Add, reorder or remove stops as needed.
itinerary.item4: Choose walking or driving, then the shortest or fastest route.
itinerary.item5: The calculated route appears in the notebook with your other map items.

organize.title: Find and organize items
organize.content: The left notebook groups project drawings and notes so you can find and manage them.
organize.item1: Items stay organized by category; create a custom group to collect different types together.
organize.item2: Use the Filter by name field to find an item.
organize.item3: A category eye shows or hides its items; each ⋮ menu offers actions for one item.
organize.item4: Select an item name to center the map on it.
organize.item5: Drag an item within its group to change its order.
organize.item6: Drag one point onto another in the notebook to create a line.

groups.title: Create and manage groups
groups.content: Collect different types of items in a group to keep the notebook easier to scan.
groups.item1: Click the folder + button next to Elements and name the group. You can create it empty and add items later.
groups.item2: A group can contain circles, lines, routes, points, polygons and notes.
groups.item3: Drag an item onto a group heading to add it, or drag it within the group to reorder its items.
groups.item4: Use the pencil to rename the group or change its items; the eye shows or hides all its items.
groups.item5: Drag an item out of the group to return it to its category, or choose Remove from group in its ⋮ menu. The folder − button dissolves the group without deleting its items.

actions.item1: Show or hide: Toggle this item on the map.
actions.item2: Nearby places: Search around this item.
actions.item3: Navigate: Move along this circle, line or route with the arrow keys.
actions.item4: Add a point on a line: Place a point at a chosen distance from one endpoint.
actions.item5: Bearings: View distances and directions to the other points.
actions.item6: Add a note: Create or edit a note attached to this item.
actions.item8: Color: Change the color of supported shapes.
actions.item9: Add center as point: Create a point at a polygon’s center.
actions.item10: Delete: Remove the item after confirmation.

importExport.title: Import and export
importExport.content: Use the Projects menu in the top bar to create or open projects, import JSON, and export project data as JSON or GPX.

gettingStartedSection.heading: 🎯 Welcome to GeoChase
gettingStartedSection.intro: GeoChase is a powerful treasure hunt solver designed to help you discover locations, analyze clues, and find hidden treasures using advanced geographic mapping and location search tools.
gettingStartedSection.whatYouCanDo: Here's what you can do to solve treasure hunts:

features.drawShapes: Draw circles, lines, points, and polygons on an interactive map
features.searchLocations: Search for locations by address and explore nearby places
features.findAlongPaths: Find locations along paths with distance and altitude filters
features.viewElevation: View elevation data for points and search results
features.savePoints: Create and reuse points for quick access across drawings
features.manageProjects: Create and manage projects with multiple drawings
features.navigate: Navigate around your shapes using arrow keys
features.exportGPX: Export as GPX for use in other mapping applications

drawingToolsSection.heading: 🔧 Drawing Tools
drawingToolsSection.intro: Create precise geometric drawings with the tools in the top toolbar.

accessing.title: Accessing Drawing Tools
accessing.description: All drawing tools are located in the top bar:
accessing.clickButtons: Click the buttons in the center of the top bar to open drawing modals
accessing.collapse: The top bar can be collapsed/expanded using the chevron button
accessing.toolsInclude: Drawing tools include: Circle, Lines (multiple types), Point, and Polygon

circle.title: 🔵 Circle
circle.description: Draw a circle on the map by specifying:
circle.name: Name: Give your circle a name (optional, auto-generated if empty)
circle.center: Center: Select from your saved points or enter coordinates manually
circle.radius: Radius: Choose km or cm when the image basemap paper equivalence is set. The conversion stays visible below the field.

line.title: ➖ Line
line.description: Draw a line with multiple modes:
line.twoPoints: Two Points: Connect two saved points
line.azimuth: Azimuth Mode: Create a line at a specific angle (azimuth) and distance
line.angle: Line at Angle: Select a start point, then a reference line passing through it. Crossing points and endpoints are supported; choose the reference when several lines meet there. Enter the angle relative to the line's start-to-end direction and the distance in the displayed unit. If no line passes through your point, create one first or use Azimuth Line for a compass bearing.
line.intersection: Intersection Mode: Draw a line through a point and extend it by the specified distance beyond that point
line.parallel: Parallel Mode: Draw a parallel line (latitude) across the map
line.freeHand: Free Hand Mode: Draw lines interactively by clicking on the map with optional azimuth lock
line.dragDrop: Drag & Drop: Drag a point to another point in the layers panel to create a line between them On the map, press and drag from a point: the line snaps to other points. Release on another point to create the line. While snapped to a point, hold Alt to lock it as a through-point and extend the line. Release Alt to resume free drawing.

point.title: 📍 Point
point.description: Mark specific locations on the map. Points can be reused as centers for circles or start/end points for lines.

polygon.title: ⬟ Polygon
polygon.description: Create an area by connecting multiple points:
polygon.selectPoints: Select Points: Choose at least 3 existing points from the map
polygon.visual: Visual: Polygons are displayed in light green with semi-transparent fill
polygon.extractCenter: Extract Center: Right-click menu to add the polygon's center as a new point
polygon.useCase: Use Case: Define search areas, mark zones of interest, or visualize boundaries

intersectionEditing.title: Adjust an existing intersection line
intersectionEditing.start: Move over the far endpoint of an intersection line. A hand cursor and a blue handle appear. Click once to start editing.
intersectionEditing.move: Move the mouse to shorten or extend the line. The start and imposed intersection stay fixed, and the endpoint follows their direction. It cannot move behind the intersection. This works in both Mercator and Geodesic projects.
intersectionEditing.snap: Near another visible line, the endpoint snaps where that line crosses the constrained path. Nearby start and end points of lines take priority, so you can join two line ends, including one you have just snapped. The imposed direction stays fixed. All line types, circle outlines and polygon edges can be used. The handle turns green and the snapped shape’s name appears.
intersectionEditing.save: The editing panel shows the distance in the active unit beyond the intersection. Click again to confirm and save it. Linked generated endpoints and dependent drawings update too.
intersectionEditing.cancel: Press Escape or click Cancel to restore the original line. Moving the endpoint previews the change; it does not save it.

crossingPoint.title: Create a point at a crossing
crossingPoint.hover: Hover where two visible lines cross in their interiors. A pin with a plus sign appears on the cursor, and a marker shows the detected crossing. This works with all line types in Mercator and Geodesic projects.
crossingPoint.create: Left-click to open the point dialog. The crossing coordinates and a name using both line names are filled in. You can edit the name, then click Add to create the point, or Cancel to leave the project unchanged.
crossingPoint.endpoints: Crossings at the start or end of either line are excluded. The usual endpoint actions remain available there.

searchSection.heading: 🔍 Search & Explore
searchSection.intro: Search for an address from the top bar, then find places near your drawings.

addressSearch.title: 🏘️ Address Search
addressSearch.description: Find locations by address and explore nearby places:
addressSearch.step1: Use the search bar in the top bar next to the GeoChase title
addressSearch.step2: Type an address, city, or place name
addressSearch.step3: View results with their coordinates in the dropdown
addressSearch.step4: Click a result to center the map on that location
addressSearch.step5: Create circles or points at the selected location

alongPath.title: 🗺️ Search Along Path
alongPath.description: Find locations near your drawn lines and points:
alongPath.step1: Draw a line or point on the map
alongPath.step2: Open the Layers panel in the left sidebar
alongPath.step3: Click the ⋮ menu on a line or point
alongPath.step4: Select Search Along from the menu
alongPath.step5: Adjust the search distance with the slider (0.5 - 25 km)
alongPath.step6: Filter results by altitude range for elevation analysis
alongPath.step7: Filter by name to find specific locations
alongPath.step8: Click results to mark them on the map

tips.title: 💡 Tips
tips.elevationData: Search results include automatic elevation data
tips.altitudeFilter: Use altitude filtering to find locations at specific elevations
tips.filtered: Results are filtered by location type (place, amenity, etc.)
tips.nameFilter: Click the name filter field to search across all results

navigationSection.heading: 🧭 Navigate Around Shapes
navigationSection.intro: Use arrow keys to move around circles and lines:

howTo.title: How to Navigate
howTo.step2: Click the ⋮ (menu) button on a circle or line

tips.title: 💡 Tips
tips.speedAdjust: Speed adjusts automatically based on zoom level
tips.zoomBehavior: Higher zoom = smaller movements, lower zoom = larger movements
tips.sidebarHide: The sidebar hides during navigation for a clearer view

toolsSection.heading: 🛠️ Tools
toolsSection.intro: Tools are quick, ephemeral helpers you can use on the map without saving anything to your project.

accessing.title: Opening the toolbar
accessing.location: Click the round tools button at the bottom-right of the map
accessing.toggle: Click it again to close the toolbar, or pick a tool to activate it

ruler.title: 📏 Ruler
ruler.description: Measure a distance and azimuth between two points without adding a line to your project.
ruler.step1: Open the toolbar and click the ruler
ruler.step2: Click the map to set the start point
ruler.step3: Move the cursor: distance and azimuth appear next to it in real time
ruler.step4: Click again to finalize the measurement; any subsequent click exits the tool (panning does not)
ruler.notSaved: Press ESC at any time to cancel. The ruler never saves a line to your layers.

layersSection.heading: 📚 Layers Panel
layersSection.intro: Manage all your drawings in the left sidebar:

accessing.title: Accessing the Layers Panel
accessing.location: The layers panel is located in the left sidebar
accessing.toggle: Toggle the left sidebar using the button on the left edge of the screen
accessing.sections: All circles, lines, points, and polygons are listed in separate sections

actions.title: Layer Actions
actions.click: Click item: Navigate to and center on the shape
actions.menu: Click ⋮ menu: Show options for the shape
actions.hideShow: 👁 Hide/Show: Toggle visibility on the map
actions.searchAlong: 🔍 Search Along: Find locations near the element (lines and points)
actions.navigate: 🧭 Navigate: Use arrow keys to move around the shape (circles and lines)
actions.bearings: 🧭 Bearings: View distances and azimuths to all other points (points only)
actions.createWith: ➕ Create with: Create new shapes from a point
actions.addCenter: ⬟ Add center as point: Extract polygon center as a new point (polygons only)
actions.addNote: Add note: Create or edit a note attached to this item
actions.color: Color: Change the color of supported shapes

dragDrop.title: Drag & Drop
dragDrop.drag: Drag a point from the Points section to another point
dragDrop.autoCreate: A line will automatically be created connecting the two points
dragDrop.naming: The line is named "Point A → Point B" with distance and azimuth info
dragDrop.fastest: This is the fastest way to connect existing points

notesSection.heading: 📝 Notes
notesSection.intro: Add notes to your drawings to document important information, observations, or clues:

howToAdd.title: How to Add Notes
howToAdd.step1: Open the Layers panel in the left sidebar
howToAdd.step2: Click the ⋮ menu on a circle, line, point, or polygon
howToAdd.step3: Select Add note from the menu
howToAdd.step4: Enter a title and content for your note
howToAdd.step5: Click Save to attach the note to the element

managing.title: Managing Notes
managing.viewOnMap: View notes on map: Notes appear as tooltips when you hover over elements on the map
managing.edit: Edit notes: Click the ⋮ menu and select "Edit note" to modify an existing note
managing.delete: Delete notes: Click the trash icon in the note tooltip or edit the note and delete it
managing.onePerElement: One note per element: Each element can have only one note
managing.saved: Notes are saved: Notes are stored with your project and included in exports

useCases.title: 💡 Use Cases
useCases.clues: Document clues or hints associated with specific locations
useCases.observations: Record observations about terrain, landmarks, or features
useCases.whyCreated: Keep track of why you created a particular circle or line
useCases.calculations: Store calculations, measurements, or reference data
useCases.reminders: Add reminders or next steps for your treasure hunt investigation

pointsSection.heading: 📍 Points
pointsSection.intro: Create and manage location markers on the map:

howToCreate.title: How to Create Points
howToCreate.step1: Right-click on the map to create a point at that location
howToCreate.step2: Or click the Point button in the top bar
howToCreate.step3: Enter a name (or leave empty for auto-generated name)
howToCreate.step4: Enter coordinates manually or select from existing points
howToCreate.step5: Click Add to create the point on the map

managing.title: Managing Points
managing.access: View all points in the Layers panel (left sidebar)
managing.view: Points show their name and coordinates
managing.edit: Edit points via the ⋮ menu → Edit
managing.delete: Delete points via the ⋮ menu → Delete
managing.sorted: Points are sorted by creation date (newest first)

useCases.title: 💡 Use Cases
useCases.lineEndpoints: Use points as line start and end points
useCases.quickReference: Mark important locations for your treasure hunt
useCases.autoGenerated: Auto-generated names use reverse geocoding to find addresses

projectsSection.heading: 🗂️ Projects
projectsSection.intro: Organize your work into separate projects:

accessing.title: Accessing Project Management
accessing.icon: Click the save icon in the top bar to access project options
accessing.dropdown: A dropdown menu shows all project actions

projectActions.title: Project Actions
projectActions.newProject: New project: choose a geographic map or an imported image, and name your project.
projectActions.loadProject: Load Project: Switch to another saved project from the modal
projectActions.exportJSON: Export JSON: Save your project as a JSON file for backup
projectActions.importJSON: Import JSON: Load a project from a JSON file
projectActions.exportGPX: Export GPX: Export your drawings as GPX for use in other apps (download icon in top bar)

features.title: Features
features.storage: Each project stores all your drawings separately
features.autoSave: Projects are saved automatically to your browser's local storage
features.renameDelete: Rename or delete projects from the Load Project modal
features.gpxExport: Export as GPX to use your drawings in other mapping applications

projection.title: Choose a project projection
projection.choice: Choose Mercator for straight lines on the map and bearings calculated as in cartes.gouv.fr, or Geodesic (WGS84) for shortest paths over the curved Earth. Geodesic paths can appear curved on the map. The background map stays the same.
projection.settings: Choose the projection when creating a project. Change it later in Project menu → Project Settings. It applies to every drawing, distance and bearing; parallels remain lines of constant latitude. Image mode uses its own planar scale.
projection.export: Your projection is saved with the project and included in JSON exports. GPX export and searches along lines follow the selected geometry. Older projects without this setting use Mercator.

pdfSection.heading: 📄 PDF Documents
pdfSection.intro: Attach PDF documents to your projects for reference while working on the map:

uploading.title: Uploading a PDF
uploading.step1: Click the PDF icon in the top bar (next to the tutorial button)
uploading.step2: If no PDF is attached, a file picker will open
uploading.step4: The PDF will be stored with your project

viewing.title: Viewing PDFs
viewing.openPanel: Click the PDF icon when a PDF is attached to open the viewer panel
viewing.resize: Drag the left edge of the panel to resize it
viewing.navigate: Use the page navigation controls to browse through pages
viewing.zoom: Use zoom controls or pinch to zoom in/out on the document

passwordProtected.title: Password-Protected PDFs
passwordProtected.step2: The password is saved so you don't need to re-enter it on reload
passwordProtected.step3: The password is stored locally and never sent to any server

features.title: Features
features.storage: PDFs are stored in your browser's IndexedDB (separate from project data)
features.perProject: Each project can have its own PDF document
features.delete: Delete a PDF by clicking the trash icon in the panel header
features.notExported: Note: PDFs are NOT included in JSON exports (to keep file sizes manageable)

keyboardShortcuts.history: Ctrl/Cmd+Z: undo; Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z or Ctrl+Y: redo. The ↶ and ↷ toolbar buttons do the same. Up to 1,000 steps for drawings, notes, groups, their visibility and projection. History is limited to 8 MiB per project; older steps are discarded when needed. History is saved locally with each project, survives reloads and is excluded from exports. Editing after undo discards the redo steps.
keyboardShortcuts.title: ⌨️ Keyboard Shortcuts
keyboardShortcuts.arrows: Arrow Keys (← →) - Navigate along circles/lines during navigation mode
keyboardShortcuts.z: Z - Toggle precision mode (magnified lens view)
keyboardShortcuts.esc: ESC - Exit navigation mode, precision mode, or cancel free hand drawing
keyboardShortcuts.rightClick: Right-click on map - Create a point at that location (also closes precision mode)
keyboardShortcuts.alt: ALT - Hold during free hand drawing to lock azimuth (only when no predefined azimuth)
keyboardShortcuts.ctrl: CTRL - Hold during free hand drawing to lock distance

precisionMode.title: 🔍 Precision Mode
precisionMode.description: Precision mode provides a magnified view of the map for accurate positioning:
precisionMode.activate: Activate: Press the Z key to toggle precision mode
precisionMode.lens: Magnified lens: A circular lens appears above your cursor showing a 2.5x magnified view
precisionMode.crosshair: Crosshair: The center crosshair helps you pinpoint exact locations
precisionMode.sameZoom: Same zoom level: The lens shows the same map zoom level, just magnified for easier viewing
precisionMode.deactivate: Deactivate: Press Z again, ESC, or right-click to exit
precisionMode.use: Use precision mode when placing points, drawing lines, or examining detailed map features

bearingsAnalysis.title: 🧭 Bearings Analysis
bearingsAnalysis.description: Analyze distances and directions between points for treasure hunt navigation:
bearingsAnalysis.openView: Open bearings view - Click ⋮ menu on any point and select "Bearings"
bearingsAnalysis.viewCalc: View calculations - See distance (km), azimuth (bearing to point), and inverse azimuth (return bearing) for all other points
bearingsAnalysis.sort: Sort data - Click column headers to sort by any field
bearingsAnalysis.navigate: Navigate quickly - Click any row to close the modal and jump to that point on the map
bearingsAnalysis.use: Use bearings to triangulate locations or verify geometric relationships between points

drawingTips.title: 🎯 Drawing Tips
drawingTips.saveFirst: Create points first - Right-click on the map to mark locations before drawing shapes
drawingTips.quickLine: Quick line creation - Drag a point to another point in the layers panel to instantly create a line

freeHandMode.title: Free Hand Mode - Draw lines interactively by clicking start and end points:
freeHandMode.setStart: Click on the map to set the start point
freeHandMode.preview: Move your mouse to preview the line with real-time distance and azimuth
freeHandMode.lockAzimuth: Hold ALT to lock the direction. On a snapped point, ALT locks that through-point and extends the line in intersection mode. This works from the Free Hand button and when dragging from a map point.
freeHandMode.lockDistance: Hold CTRL to lock the distance at the current length - useful for drawing multiple lines of the same length
freeHandMode.tooltip: The floating tooltip shows whether azimuth or distance is locked
freeHandMode.finalize: Click again to finalize the line
freeHandMode.predefined: When using predefined azimuth lock from the modal, ALT keybind is disabled

imageMapSection.title: Image basemap
imageMapSection.intro: Create a project from a scanned map or plan. The image becomes this project’s basemap and distances follow its scale.

import.title: Import an image
import.item1: Open Projects → New project, name your project and select Imported image. Click Choose an image to continue in fullscreen.
import.item2: Import a PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF or BMP file up to 25 MB. Calibration opens once the image has loaded.
import.item3: Use the mouse wheel or + and − buttons to zoom. Zooming in has no fixed cap; click and drag to pan around the image.

points.title: Calibrate with two points
points.item1: Choose Two points. Click each end of a known distance, such as the printed scale bar: two numbered crosses appear.
points.item2: Enter the real distance between the points in kilometres. For a 60 km scale bar, enter 60.
points.item3: To refine a position, click its cross and use the arrow keys: 0.1 pixel per press, or 1 pixel with Shift + arrows. The selected cross turns white.
points.item4: Replace both points clears both crosses so you can start again. Once both points are placed, clicking elsewhere does not move them.
points.item5: Optionally enter the length of the same segment on the paper map in centimetres. For example, 60 km for 6 cm means that 1 cm represents 10 km.

ratio.title: Calibrate with a known ratio
ratio.item1: Choose Known ratio to enter the number of metres represented by one pixel directly. No point placement is required.
ratio.item2: Use the ratio for your exact file, such as 169.5 m/pixel if verified for that scan. Resizing an image changes its ratio; its filename alone is no guarantee.
ratio.item3: To enable centimetres, optionally fill in Km per 1 cm: enter 10 for a 1:1,000,000 map. The summary shows the resulting ratio and equivalence.

usage.title: Use and change the image basemap
usage.item1: After calibration, click Create project. To adjust the scale later, use Recalibrate in the toolbar, then Save. Back to project returns to the initial choice before creation.
usage.item2: With the paper equivalence set, distances show kilometres alongside their equivalent in centimetres on the map. In radius and distance fields, choose km or cm: switching converts the value without changing the distance, and the other unit stays visible below the field. Without a paper equivalence, inputs use kilometres.
usage.item3: Measurements follow the image scale, like a ruler on the paper map. Image mode does not georeference the scan and hides address search; there is no city calibration.
usage.item4: The image and its calibration are saved locally in this browser for this project. The image file and calibration are not included in JSON exports: keep the original file and your calibration values.
usage.item5: The basemap type is chosen at creation: image projects have no basemap selector. To work on a geographic map, create or open a project of that type. Recalibrate is only shown for image projects.

analysis.content: Figures come from the app’s calculations and public services (IGN, OpenStreetMap, Wikimedia), not from the model’s estimate.
analysis.item1: The ground distance and bearing, computed with the project’s projection.
analysis.item2: Start, end, minimum and maximum elevation, ascent and descent, plus a point at the summit. “What is the elevation of these points?” works too.
analysis.item3: An IGN route with its real distance and duration. Say “by car” or “fastest” if needed.
analysis.item4: After you paste a photo, the assistant fetches photos of these places from Wikimedia and compares them. It names the places without a photo and never draws a conclusion about a place it has not seen.
analysis.label1: “What distance and bearing between Crossing 1 and Melun?”
analysis.label2: “Give me the elevation profile of this line and place its highest point.”
analysis.label3: “Draw the walking route from Fontainebleau to Melun.”
analysis.label4: “Compare my photo with the churches in the project.”
analysis.title: Examples: measurements and analysis

attachments.content: Up to 4 attachments per message: PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF images and unencrypted PDFs, up to 10 MB each.
attachments.item1: Paste a screenshot or an image into the input field (Ctrl+V), or use the paperclip to choose a file.
attachments.item2: The map button attaches the current view with its geographic bounds, for instance to ask “What does this area show?”.
attachments.item3: When the project has a PDF, its button attaches it in one click, for instance for “Place the places named in this document”.
attachments.item4: The last 3 attachments are sent again with the following messages, so you can ask several questions about the same image. They cost each time they are sent: Forget removes them.
attachments.title: Attachments and memory

connect.content: The assistant uses your own OpenAI, Anthropic (Claude) or Google Gemini API key. Requests are billed to your account by that provider; the key stays in this browser and is only sent to it.
connect.item1: Click the magic wand at the top right to open the Assistant panel.
connect.item2: Paste your key: the provider is detected when possible, otherwise choose it. Click Load models.
connect.item3: Choose a model and, when it allows it, the reasoning effort. Auto suits most requests; high effort is slower and costs more, but is more reliable for multi-step constructions and image calibration. Then click Open conversation.
connect.item4: Tick Remember the key only on a personal device. Forget key removes it from this browser.
connect.title: Connect the assistant

constructions.content: The assistant computes each construction with the same rules as the manual tools and the project’s projection: it never works out coordinates by itself.
constructions.item1: Two circles, then their crossings named “1” and “2”. Add “keep the northern one” to keep only one.
constructions.item2: A line between the two points, then a point placed on it. Then “measure it from the other end” moves it while keeping the same fraction (preview to confirm).
constructions.item3: A line centred on the midpoint, every point of which is equally far from both towns. Same idea for a midpoint, the centroid of several points, or an angle bisector.
constructions.item4: The side follows the direction you give (north, south, east, west). Without a direction or a length, the assistant asks for it.
constructions.item5: It extends the line, and finds the crossing even when the drawn segments do not touch.
constructions.item6: A polygon with its area and the list of points inside it. Also works for points lying in two circles at once.
constructions.label1: “Find the points 12 km from Fontainebleau and 10 km from Melun.”
constructions.label2: “Draw the Fontainebleau–Melun line and put a point one third of the way from Melun.”
constructions.label3: “Draw the perpendicular bisector of Fontainebleau and Melun over 20 km.”
constructions.label4: “From this point on the line, draw the perpendicular towards the north over 5 km.”
constructions.label5: “Extend this line by 6 km and give me where it crosses the other one.”
constructions.label6: “Make a zone with these three points and tell me which points are inside.”
constructions.title: Examples: constructions

edits.content: The assistant remembers the elements of the conversation: “it”, “this circle”, “the other end” refer to the elements it just talked about.
edits.item1: Renames the last element mentioned, keeping its links with other elements.
edits.item2: Changes the radius of the existing circle; the preview shows the old one in red and the new one in purple before applying.
edits.item3: Only the element you pointed at is deleted, after confirmation. A point that forms a zone, or a line other constructions depend on, is refused while those exist.
edits.item4: Colours of lines, circles, zones and routes, and visibility of any element. Points keep their style.
edits.item5: Creates the note, or adds to it if the element already has one.
edits.item6: Downloads the GPX file once the request is applied.
edits.label4: “Make the Melun circle red and hide the route.”
edits.label5: “Add a note to this point: main candidate.”
edits.title: Examples: correcting and organising

how.content: Creations and renames apply directly at the end of the request. Deletions and moves are first previewed on the map (purple: proposed, red: before or removed) and wait for you to click Apply changes. The conversation is kept for each project.
how.item1: Click a point, line or circle on the map or in the notebook before writing: “this point” or “this line” then refers to it. The selection is shown above the input field.
how.item2: Created or modified elements are listed under the answer: click them to centre the map. The map also frames what the request added.
how.item3: When several elements match, the assistant offers clickable choices instead of guessing. Clicking a choice sends the request again with that element.
how.item4: Undo, under the conversation, reverts the whole last request. Stop interrupts a running request without applying anything.
how.title: How it works

assistantSection.intro: Describe in plain words what you want on the map: the assistant does it with GeoChase’s own tools, without inventing coordinates. It prepares everything, then applies the request in one go when it has finished; Undo reverts the whole request.

limits.item1: A request has at most 12 exchanges with the model and 36 actions. Split long work into several messages.
limits.item2: IGN geocoding, routes and elevations cover France. OpenStreetMap and Wikimedia depend on contributions: a little-known place may be missing.
limits.item3: Each request sends the project’s elements (names, coordinates, notes) to the provider. Images and PDFs are only sent when you attach them.
limits.item4: The assistant does not work in an image project, nor while a drawing tool or a dialog is open: finish those first.
limits.title: Good to know

overlay.content: The assistant can place an image overlay (added with the Image button), a PDF or image attached to the conversation, or the project PDF. It looks at the image with a grid, zooms in on the details you describe, checks its positions with markers, then computes the placement, rotation and size. An imported PDF keeps its page size (21 × 29.7 cm for A4), so a scale such as 1:1,000,000 gives its true size.
overlay.item1: The first anchor lands exactly on Fontainebleau and the image is rotated so the second points at Chambord. Because the scale is fixed, the second anchor may land slightly off: the assistant reports that gap and the scale the two anchors alone would give.
overlay.item2: Both anchors land exactly on their places and the scale is derived. Moving an image that is already there goes through the preview (red outline before, purple after) to confirm.
overlay.item3: With three anchors or more, it computes the best fit and reports each one’s gap: a much larger gap points to an anchor placed or described wrongly.
overlay.item4: Choose visible, unique details (a tip, a corner, a crossing) and precise places: “Château de Chambord” rather than “Chambord” if the castle is what matters. For a photo or scan, give its printed width if you want to force a scale.
overlay.label1: “Put the top of the left pole on Fontainebleau and the mark above the round thing on Chambord, at 1:1,000,000 scale.”
overlay.label2: “Calibrate it again without forcing the scale.”
overlay.label3: “Calibrate this plan with the station, the church and the bridge.”
overlay.title: Example: calibrating an image or PDF on the map

places.content: Simply write the places you want. Geocoding covers France; a town is placed at its geographic centre.
places.item1: Three points, one at the centre of each town. If a name matches several towns, the assistant asks which one.
places.item2: For a historical fact, it first searches the web for sources, tells tombs, remains and memorials apart, then attaches the sources as a note on the new point.
places.item3: It queries OpenStreetMap around the Melun point and places what it finds. Also works with “inside this circle”, and for fountains, peaks, castles, lighthouses, museums…
places.item4: A point at a given distance and bearing, without drawing a line.
places.label3: “Place the churches within 3 km of Melun.”
places.label4: “Put a point 3 km north-east of Fontainebleau.”
places.title: Examples: placing places
